title: Toto Wolff needs 'more proof' from Mercedes upgrade to 'feel warm and fuzzy'
excerpt:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has conceded he needs "more proof" that the upgrades on Kimi Antonelli's car are working before feeling content about the situation.

Mercedes unveiled an update package on the W17 at last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, leaving many of their F1 rivals fearful the team would take another leap forward after dominating this season.

Instead, Mercedes were not as competitive as had been expected, with fingers being pointed at the conditions and the abrasive asphalt at the Sepang International Circuit.

Heading into this weekend in Singapore, and knowing George Russell would be hit with a major power unit penalty, the team has so far run two different packages, reverting to the spec on the Briton's car that helped him dominate in Azerbaijan, whilst leaving title-leading team-mate Antonelli on the new spec.

After first practice, Mercedes then placed the old front wing on Antonelli's car, believing it to be a step forward.

In sprint qualifying, Russell and Antonelli qualified second and seventh; for the grand prix, Antonelli was fourth fastest, Russell sixth, although he will be demoted to the back of the pack.

Summing up the event so far as "complicated" given his team has "two different cars running", speaking to Sky Sports F1, Wolff added: "On Kimi's side, the update seems to have worked now.

"He and his engineers have dialled out the problems, and we got closer and closer. Eventually, we're missing a tenth and a half or two tenths, and that is at least positive for qualifying."

As to whether he was 'feeling a bit more warm and fuzzy' towards the upgrade, Wolff replied: "It will take more proof of concept until I'm feeling warm and fuzzy, but we will have more data tomorrow in the race."

[Article continues below]

Wolff - 'I didn't think it was him'

Wolff at least hailed the performance of Russell in qualifying after crashing out of the sprint earlier in the day whilst leading at the end of lap one.

In wet conditions, Russell nailed his start off the line and surged past polesitter Max Verstappen in his Red Bull on the short run-down to Turn 1, only to then lose the rear of his car after running over a painted kerb as he turned onto the start-finish straight.

Wolff was stunned to see Russell make such a mistake, but at least pleased he recovered to execute a solid qualifying in a car not fully rebuilt.

"When I saw the yellow coming out, I didn't think it was him because I couldn't imagine that George would make such a mistake because it hasn't happened for a long time," said Wolff. "The last one was in Singapore, in the race with Lewis [Hamilton] maybe, so very, very unusual.

"Fair enough, the power kicked in at a moment where he didn't expect it, and he was on the white line. Running first is always tricky because you're looking at how fast you can go through the corners, so not at all like George, but anything can happen.

"The mechanics then did an unbelievable job in putting the car together, but maybe at the end, we didn't have all of the sensors on the car, and it didn't feel as good as it did before, but George did a really good job."

title: McLaren issue Lando Norris-Oscar Piastri warning after Sprint meltdown
excerpt:
McLaren has issued a stark warning to Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri after the two title rivals collided on the last lap of the Singapore Sprint, with team principal Andrea Stella making clear that nobody at the team is bigger than the collective cause.

The incident wrecked what should have been a productive sprint for the Woking-based outfit. McLaren went into the 100 km race at Marina Bay in position to bank solid points at a track where victory was out of reach, only for Norris and Piastri to make contact at Turn 5 and both spin.

Norris salvaged just a single point in eighth, while Piastri failed to finish, although was classified 14th due to the timing of the accident.

Stella did not hide his frustration, telling Sky F1 that the situation would be dealt with behind-the-scenes in private.

"The sprint race was a race that was giving us some good points in a moment in which we are not in condition to win," begun Stella. "Still, we were in condition to score good points, and we saw two McLarens having contact, basically going out of the race.

"Lando scored one point, but definitely that's not enough. And seeing two McLarens making contact like that is simply not acceptable. This is something that we will discuss with our drivers. We will do it in private.

"We will reiterate that the team interest is far bigger than any of us. There's no ego, there's no person that is bigger than the interest of the McLaren Formula 1 team.

"This will be reiterated. I'm sure, like always, there will be conversations that will lead to the team being more united and even stronger."

Lando Norris insists both McLaren drivers to blame

Norris, who leads the McLaren intra-team battle, confirmed that himself and Piastri had already sat down to clear the air once the dust settled on the sprint.

Asked what the discussion with the team was like, Norris told select media, including RacingNews365, that the mood in the camp was far from celebratory.

"As you probably expect, no one's very happy. I'm not happy, Oscar wasn't happy," said Norris. "None of us wanted it to go that way.

"There was things both of us could have done better, and yeah, we spoke about it and we moved on."

title: Red Bull engine penalty looming for Isack Hadjar as 'everything's breaking apart'
excerpt:
Isack Hadjar declared himself to be 'pissed off' following a day to forget for the Red Bull driver after limping out of both the Singapore Sprint and qualifying for the grand prix.

In the sprint race earlier in the day, Hadjar was forced to pull his RB22 off the circuit due to a power unit problem as the field toured behind the safety car following a crash at the end of lap one involving George Russell in his Mercedes.

During the interval between the sprint and qualifying at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, the Red Bull mechanics replaced PU components with others from the pool, allowing Hadjar to start qualifying. The French-Algerian driver even thanked the team as he returned to the track.

It was not long, however, before he encountered further issues. Initially, he was forced to stop on track, but managed to get the car going again and return to the garage. Despite another attempt to post a lap, Hadjar then complained of a gearbox problem which proved terminal.

Asked of Hadjar whether he could digest his situation more easily as the gearbox issue was not his problem, speaking to Sky Sports F1, he replied: "No, I want to drive.

"Honestly, I don't care about P22. I just want to get out there and do my thing. I have plenty of soft tyres in the garage right now that aren't going to be used, and that's what pisses me off the most right now. I just want to be there fighting with the other guys."

With Hadjar to start at the back of the grid on a track where it is notoriously difficult to overtake, he confirmed the team is likely to fit a fresh power unit ahead of the race, which would lead to a pit lane start.

"We need new stuff, and tomorrow is an opportunity, obviously, because everything's breaking apart this weekend," he said.

"So, yeah, we need a fresh restart."

title: Charles Leclerc reveals 'weird' Ferrari issue in Max Verstappen defeat
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc has revealed his Ferrari suffered from a "weird" brake issue during Singapore Grand Prix qualifying, as the Monegasque narrowly missed out on pole position to Max Verstappen.

Leclerc qualified second at Marina Bay, just 0.054s behind the Red Bull driver, who took pole with a lap of 1m 31.373. Lewis Hamilton completed a strong session for Ferrari in third, with Kimi Antonelli fourth for Mercedes.

Despite the final result, Leclerc's path through qualifying was far from straightforward. The 28-year-old struggled through the early stages at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, a track notorious for punishing braking zones.

It was only in the final runs of Q3 that Leclerc managed to put together a lap good enough to challenge for top spot, though he conceded the margin to Verstappen ultimately came down to his own mistakes rather than pace alone.

"The good lap was on the right lap at the end, but I had a lot of struggles during this qualifying," said Leclerc.

"Q1 and Q2 were very difficult. I had some weird things going on with the brakes, the car pulling a bit under braking, which is not so nice on a track like here.

"But then in Q3, the lap was ok. I did some mistakes. I think there was a potential to be on pole today but Max just did a better job."

Charles Leclerc convinced Singapore pole was possible

Leclerc also addressed suggestions that he and Hamilton had settled on similar set-up directions for Ferrari across the weekend, with the Briton splitting the Red Bull and Ferrari drivers in third.

Asked if himself and Hamilton converged on set-up, Leclerc said: "Well, I guess, yeah. On my side, I changed the car a little bit to make sure we got the final fine-tuning right.

"I was relatively happy with the car yesterday, so we changed a few things, but not so much. At the end of the day, it was just a bit of misjudgement in Q3 with the wing.

"Maybe we could have done a bit of a better job, but I think if you ask all the drivers on the grid, everybody can find something on that last lap in Q3."

title: Lewis Hamilton plots against Max Verstappen as Ferrari plan comes together
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton is plotting to work strategically with Charles Leclerc to overcome polesitter Max Verstappen at the Singapore Grand Prix.

Hamilton will line up third at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, behind the four-time F1 drivers' champion and his Ferrari team-mate.

The British driver looked right in contention to top the grid-setting session after a sublime effort in Q2, but a couple of corrections on each of his Q3 laps left him unable to extract the maximum from the SF-26 underneath him.

"Another difficult Q3. Congrats to Max, he did a great job," Hamilton said after getting out of his car. "We made some changes going into qualifying. The car was feeling so much better, and I really felt like she had more in her; we were pushing her more and more through the laps and through the sessions.

"Q1 and Q2 we were awesome. We got to Q3, and I snapped into Turn 1, 3 and was two tenths down. The rest of the lap was good.

"And the last lap I just struggled with snapping. There's a real fine line with our car where it's over the edge or under the limit.

"Finding that sweet spot is very difficult. I probably had it in the first two [sessions] but you have to look to the progress of the track, the grip coming up and you have to kind of react to that.

"With hindsight, maybe I shouldn't have, so it wasn't great enough with myself."

Hamilton's plan to fight Verstappen

Hamilton was quick to praise the impressive pace of the RB22, before sharing a glimpse of the potential tactics Ferrari might employ to stop Verstappen from finally winning in Singapore.

"Red Bull has done a fantastic job," Hamilton added. "They've done a great job with their engine, but I think also with their car; it's obviously a great team, and I think they brought an upgrade in Baku, which has really put them at the front.

"And I think it's really still a good result for us to have two Ferraris up there. We could definitely, hopefully, work as a team tomorrow to try and hold on to Max and put them under pressure.

"I think that's the only way it's gonna be. I'm sure it's gonna be fast, but hopefully, together as a team, we can potentially... Who knows? We'll see if we can get ahead of them."

title: Max Verstappn lands 'the one I wanted' after close Singapore GP qualifying fight
excerpt:
Max Verstappen finally clinched "the one I wanted" by taking pole position for the Singapore Grand Prix, and the 50th of his F1 career.

Around a Marina Bay Street Circuit, where Verstappen and Red Bull have predominantly struggled, this weekend he has tamed the streets of Singapore by claiming a sprint win from pole, and now pole for the grand prix on Sunday.

It was a close-run duel, with Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton initially going head to head. The seven-time F1 champion had the edge over his big rival in Q1 and Q2, only to seemingly fight more with his SF-26 in Q3 to finish third behind the Dutchman and his Scuderia team-mate.

"Just the margins were very close between us throughout the whole of qualifying," said Verstappen on Sky Sports F1. "Very happy to be on pole because this is the one I wanted, so very happy.

"The car has been really strong all weekend. Always things that can be better, but it was enough for pole, so happy with that.

"[There are] New regulations, and our car now works a little bit differently compared to the previous regulations where we were stronger in different areas of a corner, but yeah, we take it.

"We have been on a positive trend, so for us, it's very special to take pole here."

In the sprint race, Verstappen bemoaned his start as "horrendous" and called on Red Bull to get to the bottom of the issue.

As for what start he can expect for the grand prix, he said: "You have to look at it positively. It cannot get worse. It can only get better, so we'll see how it goes tomorrow."

title: Max Verstappen sets up showdown with destiny after heroic Singapore pole
excerpt:
Max Verstappen stormed to pole position at the Singapore Grand Prix in a closely fought, high-octane grid-setting session under the lights of the Marina Bay Street Circuit, posting a 1:31.373.

It was Verstappen's 50th pole in F1, and it puts him on track to finally conquer the last circuit — other than the new Madring — he has yet to triumph at. He has only ever led three grand prix laps in Singapore.

Charles Leclerc qualified second, half a tenth slower but 69 milliseconds ahead of Lewis Hamilton at F1's original night race, whilst Kimi Antonelli and Lando Norris rounded out the top five.

Isack Hadjar was the big-name scalp from Q1, when a gearbox failure ended what had already been a messy segment for the Red Bull driver.

He will be joined at the tail of the field by George Russell, who has taken a grid penalty for a power unit change, and Fernando Alonso, who has claimed he will also take a grid drop, having been knocked out of Q1 too.

The Mercedes driver was sixth fastest in the Southeast Asian city-state, with Oscar Piastri seventh.

Pierre Gasly beat the Racing Bulls pair of Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad in the best of the rest battle.
